_meta.goal: fix the four measured cost-efficiency defects found in the cost audit: invisible waste in af cost, a torn/silently-empty state ledger, agent work discarded on a gate failure (855.9s measured), and crashes bypassing the retry budget

tasks.title: Make af cost surface wasted spend and its causes (cost_report_surfaces_wasted_spend) so failed attempts stop being invisible in the cost ledger
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn cost_report_surfaces_wasted_spend' tests/cli.rs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL (cost efficiency): `af cost` is the only cost ledger agentflow has, and today it cannot show WASTE. A failed attempt's wall-clock is indistinguishable from productive spend: the report only prints per-task totals and a global TOTAL. Fix that, because waste you cannot see is waste you cannot reduce.

BACKGROUND (measured over the six dogfooding campaigns: 34 attempts, 14374.5s of agent wall-clock): 855.9s (6.0%) was spent on attempts whose outcome was `failed`. One of them was a gate flake the agent could not have avoided. The data to surface this already exists on every receipt — `outcome` ("merged" | "failed"), `error` (the failure's first line), and `wall_clock_s` — it is simply never reported.

REQUIREMENTS in `run::cost` (src/run.rs):
1. Add a waste section to the report. It MUST be computed from the SAME `selected` receipts the rest of the report uses, so the existing `--last` / `--since` / `--task` windows narrow the waste figure too. Do NOT recompute from all receipts.
2. A total line giving, in this order: wasted seconds (one decimal), the failed attempt count, the total attempt count in the window, and the wasted percentage. Suggested shape (exact wording is yours, keep the numbers exact):
     WASTED: 855.9s on 1 of 34 attempt(s) (6.0%)
3. A per-reason breakdown, one row per distinct failure reason, each with its summed seconds and its attempt count. Derive the reason key from the receipt's `error` field: first line only, trimmed, truncated to a stable length (e.g. 48 chars), and the literal key `unknown` when `error` is None. Group equal keys together and order deterministically: descending summed seconds, ties broken by the reason string ascending.
     WASTED BY REASON
       acceptance gate failed      855.9s  (1)
       agent exited                12.0s   (1)
4. Zero-failure window must be explicit and must not divide by zero or panic — print the line with 0.0s / 0 of N. The reason breakdown may be omitted when there are no failures.
5. Do not change any existing line: the per-task rows, the `TOTAL: ...s across N receipt(s)` line and the per-worker trust table must stay byte-identical, and the trust/table math must keep using `selected`. Existing tests assert on these strings — do not break them.
6. Keep it std-only (no new dependencies) and keep the function testable. If the grouping logic needs a helper, make it a small private function.

TEST in tests/cli.rs — add `#[test] fn cost_report_surfaces_wasted_spend()`. Follow the existing cost tests in that file exactly: `Cli::new_with_tasks(...)`, `cli.settings()`, `Store::new(st.state_dir.clone()).append_receipt(...)`, then `cli.af(&["cost", ...])` and assert on the returned (exit code, output). Seed receipts with a mix: at least two merged and two failed attempts with DIFFERENT error strings and known wall-clock values, e.g. failed 100.0s error "acceptance gate failed (exit 1): boom" and failed 20.0s error "agent exited NonZero (code 7)". Assert:
   - the waste line reports the exact summed failed seconds (120.0s), the failed attempt count, the total attempt count and the percentage;
   - the reason breakdown lists BOTH reasons with their own summed seconds;
   - `af cost --last` narrows the waste figure to the failures surviving that window (prove the composition rather than merely restating the full-window number);
   - a window whose selected receipts contain no failures reports 0.0s without panicking.
The waste section must appear for a plain `af cost` with no flags.

DOCS: add a short paragraph to README.md documenting the waste section and that it is computed over the same window as the rest of the report.

tasks.title: Make run-state.json writable from many threads without tearing, and stop treating a corrupt state file as an empty campaign (concurrent_saves_never_tear_the_state_file, corrupt_state_is_an_error_not_an_empty_campaign)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn concurrent_saves_never_tear_the_state_file' tests/state_race.rs && grep -q 'fn corrupt_state_is_an_error_not_an_empty_campaign' tests/state_strict.rs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL (cost + data integrity): make `run-state.json` safe to write from several threads, and make a corrupt state file IMPOSSIBLE to mistake for an empty campaign. This is the single most expensive latent bug in the codebase.

BUG 1 - the write race (reproduced): `Store::save` writes to `run-state.json.tmp{std::process::id()}`. That filename is IDENTICAL for every thread in the process. `std::fs::write` opens with truncate, so concurrent writers do not each get their own temp file - they truncate and interleave one shared file. The first `rename` can install a byte-mixed document while the second fails ENOENT (swallowed by `let _ = ...save(...)`). Concurrent writers are real: `run::run_loop` spawns one `execute::execute_task` thread per task, each calls `execute::record_phase` (load-modify-save), and `run_loop` itself calls `save` when dispatching and `reap` calls it again on completion. A 6-thread x 150-save probe measured 651 of 900 saves returning Err and 86 concurrent reads seeing unparseable JSON. (The doc comment on `execute::record_phase` claims a losing write is "superseded whole, never torn" - that claim is false; do not preserve it. Correct it if you leave the comment in place.)

FIX 1a - unique temp path per write: include a process-global atomic counter (and/or the thread id) so no two writers ever share a temp file. The final `rename` must stay the atomic install step, and the temp file must be removed if the write fails.

FIX 1b - durability: fsync the temp file before renaming so a power loss cannot leave a truncated or empty ledger. Use std only: `std::fs::File::create` + `write_all` + `sync_all`. Do not add dependencies.

BUG 2 - silent campaign reset (reproduced): `Store::load` is `serde_json::from_str(&s).unwrap_or_default()`. A torn or corrupt `run-state.json` therefore becomes an EMPTY map with no warning, so every `done` task looks `ready` and `af run` re-buys every agent invocation. Demonstrated on a finished 4-task campaign (2979.9s of agent compute): truncating run-state.json in half made `af status` report all four tasks `Ready` and `af run --dry-run` re-dispatch all four, silently.

FIX 2 - an explicitly fallible read: add `pub fn load_checked(&self) -> io::Result<HashMap<String, TaskStatus>>` (name it as you see fit, keep it on `Store` and mirror it on the `StateStore` trait only if that does not break `tests/conformance.rs`) which:
   - returns Ok(empty) when the state file does NOT exist - a fresh campaign is legitimate, not an error;
   - returns Err whose message NAMES the offending path (and the parse problem) when the file exists but cannot be parsed or is not a task map;
   - returns Ok(map) otherwise.
Then make `run::run_loop` and `run::dry_run` use it and REFUSE TO START on Err: print a clear `config error: ...` line and `return 2` instead of dispatching anything. This is the money-saving behaviour: never silently re-run a campaign because its ledger is unreadable. Do not delete, rename or overwrite the corrupt file - it is evidence, and the user may want to repair it.
Keep `Store::load` for the read-only display paths (`run::status_board`, `run::status_json`, `run::attach`, and reap's journal reconciliation) so you do not churn every call site, but make it LOUD: when the file exists and cannot be parsed it must emit a warning to stderr naming the file. It must never silently present a corrupt ledger as a fresh one.

TESTS (both files new, both hermetic - a unique directory per test nested under its own per-test subdir, cleaned up at the end; std + the crate only, no new dependencies):
1. tests/state_race.rs - `#[test] fn concurrent_saves_never_tear_the_state_file()`. Spawn at least 4 threads that each call `Store::save` at least 100 times on the SAME state dir. Make the payloads differ a lot in size between threads (e.g. give some threads a long `last_error` string and others a short one) so interleaving damage is actually detectable - identical tiny payloads can hide the bug. While they write, a concurrent reader repeatedly reads the status file and parses it with `serde_json::from_str::<HashMap<String, TaskStatus>>`. Assert BOTH: zero `save` calls returned Err, and zero reads were unparseable. Keep the whole test to a few seconds.
2. tests/state_strict.rs - `#[test] fn corrupt_state_is_an_error_not_an_empty_campaign()`. Assert (a) a missing state file is Ok(empty) - a fresh campaign must still work; (b) a valid state file round-trips (including a Done task); (c) a truncated/garbage state file returns Err whose message names the path, NOT Ok(empty); (d) the decisive one: build a minimal `Config` + `Settings` (`agentflow::config::load` on temp JSON files, `Settings { state_dir, .. }`) whose state dir contains a corrupt `run-state.json`, and assert `agentflow::run::run_loop(&cfg, &st, &RunOptions::default()) == 2` - i.e. the orchestrator refuses to re-dispatch and exits 2 rather than re-buying the campaign. Also assert `run::dry_run(&cfg, &st) == 2` so the displayed plan can never disagree with reality.

DO NOT BREAK: `src/state.rs`'s existing unit tests (`torn_write_never_corrupts`, `legacy_receipt_without_outcome_is_merged`, `receipts_append_and_aggregate`, the phase tests) and `tests/conformance.rs` (the generic `StateStore` suite) must all stay green. `torn_write_never_corrupts` writes a stale `run-state.json.tmp12345` and asserts the real file wins - your unique naming must keep that true.

tasks.title: Stop discarding the agent's committed work when the acceptance gate fails: a retry with durable agent work re-runs only the gate and never the agent (gate_flake_retry_does_not_rerun_the_agent, gate_failure_keeps_the_agents_committed_branch)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn gate_flake_retry_does_not_rerun_the_agent' tests/e2e.rs && grep -q 'fn gate_failure_keeps_the_agents_committed_branch' tests/e2e.rs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL (cost efficiency - the biggest measured leak): when the acceptance gate fails, agentflow currently THROWS AWAY the agent's paid work and re-runs the agent from scratch on the retry. Stop that. A gate flake cost 855.9s of agent compute in the dogfooding campaigns (6.0% of all spend) because the agent had already succeeded, committed its work and journaled `AttemptPhase::AgentDone` - and then `cleanup()` ran `worktree::remove`, which does `git worktree remove --force` AND `git branch -D`.

CURRENT CONTROL FLOW (`src/execute.rs::execute_attempt`): (1) `worktree::create` - which itself does `git branch -D <branch>` for the id and then `worktree add -b <branch>`; (2) `record_phase(Spawned)`; (3) run the agent; on failure `cleanup()` (worktree + branch deleted) -> Failed; (4) scope check; on violation `cleanup()` -> Failed; (5) `record_phase(AgentDone)`; (6) run the gate; ON GATE FAILURE `cleanup()` -> Failed  <-- this is the leak; (7) `record_phase(GatePassed)`; (8) `worktree::merge`; on failure `cleanup()` -> Failed.
Note `cleanup()` = `worktree::remove`, which destroys both the worktree dir and the branch, and `worktree::create` would destroy the branch again anyway.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR:
1. A GATE failure must NOT destroy the attempt branch. The agent's committed work is durable and is precisely what the journal's `AgentDone` records. Removing the worktree DIRECTORY is fine; deleting the BRANCH is not. Keep the agent-failure, scope-violation and merge-failure paths deleting the branch as they do today (in those cases there is no verified durable work to keep).
2. On a retry, decide from durable evidence whether the agent must run again. If the attempt branch exists AND carries at least one commit not reachable from the base branch (compare against the base branch, e.g. `git rev-list --count <base>..<branch>` or an equivalent check), then the agent's work is already durable: attach a worktree to that EXISTING branch and re-run ONLY the acceptance gate. DO NOT invoke the agent. The agent step must be skipped entirely.
3. Re-run the scope check on the reused work before merging. A change that is out of scope must never reach the base branch, even when it arrives via the reuse path.
4. If the gate fails AGAIN on a gate-only retry, then delete the branch so the NEXT attempt is a full agent run. This bounds the optimisation: at most one cheap gate re-run before paying for the agent again, so genuinely wrong agent work is still recoverable. (Infer this locally: if this attempt did not run the agent and the gate failed, the branch must be dropped.)
5. If the branch is absent, or carries no commit beyond the base branch, fall back to exactly today's behaviour: a fresh agent run. Legitimacy matters more than cleverness - never let a missing artifact silently produce a "verified" merge.
6. Add the worktree helper(s) this needs in `src/worktree.rs` rather than open-coding git in execute.rs, e.g. an `attach`-style function that reuses an existing branch instead of `create`'s branch-deleting behaviour, and a way to remove the worktree WITHOUT deleting the branch. Keep `create`/`remove` semantics for their existing callers and honour the house style: trusted subprocess via the crate's own git helper with a hard timeout, `git branch -D` only where deletion is intended.
7. Keep the per-attempt receipt and the attempt numbering exactly as they are: one receipt per attempt with the real outcome (`failed` for a gate-only retry that fails, `merged` when it lands), so `af cost` and the router stay correct.

TESTS in tests/e2e.rs (use the existing `fixture(...)`, `gate_cmd(...)`, `worker_json(max_attempts)` helpers and the `ENV_GUARD` mutex like the neighbouring tests):
1. `#[test] fn gate_flake_retry_does_not_rerun_the_agent()` - THE decisive test. Build a gate that fails the FIRST time it runs and passes the second, using a counter file that lives OUTSIDE the repo (an absolute path under a temp dir), e.g.: `n=$(cat <abs>/COUNT 2>/dev/null || echo 0); n=$((n+1)); echo $n > <abs>/COUNT; test $n -ge 2`. Use `max_attempts` 3. Then assert: `run::run_loop(...) == 0`; the task is `Done`; its `attempts` is 2; the agent's artifact was merged into the base repo. And the key assertion: count how many times the agent actually ran.
   HOW TO COUNT AGENT INVOCATIONS: `execute_attempt` appends the literal marker line `-- agent --` to the task's log immediately before spawning the agent CLI, and a gate-only retry never reaches that code. So read `st.state_dir.join("logs").join("<id>.log")` and count `log.matches("-- agent --").count()`. Assert it equals exactly 1 (the agent ran once, the gate ran twice). Under the current code this count is 2, which is the bug.
2. `#[test] fn gate_failure_keeps_the_agents_committed_branch()` - a gate that ALWAYS fails with `max_attempts` 1 must leave the task `Failed` (exit code 2 from run_loop) AND leave branch `<branch_prefix>/<id>` present with at least one commit beyond the base branch. Use `worktree::branch_exists`-equivalent evidence: `git rev-parse --verify refs/heads/tf/<id>` in the fixture repo, and `git rev-list --count main..tf/<id>` > 0. Today the branch is gone, which is the data-loss half of the bug.

DO NOT BREAK: `retry_after_gate_failure_runs_fresh_attempts_until_it_passes` (tests/e2e.rs) drives a gate that fails twice then passes, with `max_attempts` 3, and asserts `attempts == 3` plus receipt outcomes `["failed","failed","merged"]`. Under the required behaviour those assertions still hold - attempts still counts dispatches and there is still one receipt per attempt - only the agent invocation count changes. Verify that explicitly with `cargo test --test e2e retry_after_gate_failure` and keep it green rather than deleting it. Also keep `agent_failure_fails_task`, `retry_runs_up_to_max_attempts` (an AGENT failure must still re-run the agent on a fresh attempt) and `merge_conflict_fails_the_task_branch_cleanly` green.

tasks.title: Make an interrupted attempt consume the retry budget so a crash loop cannot re-buy the agent forever (interrupted_attempt_consumes_the_retry_budget)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn interrupted_attempt_consumes_the_retry_budget' src/run.rs && cargo test --lib interrupted_attempt_consumes_the_retry_budget -- --exact && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL (cost efficiency): `max_attempts` is the only retry budget agentflow has, and a CRASHED attempt does not consume it. `reap` is the sole writer of `TaskStatus::attempts`, and `heal_stale_attempt` (the startup heal for a stale `running` entry) rewinds the task to `Ready` WITHOUT incrementing it - the existing unit test even asserts "attempt count is preserved". So an attempt that dies before it can be reaped (OOM killer, reboot, kill -9, a long agent run the machine cannot hold) is FREE: a crash loop re-buys the agent invocation forever, never reaching `max_attempts`.

REQUIRED INVARIANT: `attempts` counts attempts that were STARTED. An interrupted attempt was started, so it counts. After healing, a task must have consumed the budget for that attempt.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR in `src/run.rs`:
1. `heal_stale_attempt` must count the interrupted attempt: increment `attempts` for the stale `running` entry it heals, and then apply the budget - if `attempts >= max_attempts` the task becomes `Failed` (with a `last_error` that says the run was interrupted and the budget is exhausted); otherwise it becomes `Ready` as today. Do this consistently for every resume outcome (RerunAgent, and the `handled == false` fallback); a resume path that COMPLETES the task (RerunGate/MergeOnly that lands or merges) may leave the task Done and the count is then irrelevant.
2. Keep the invariant that a task can never exceed `max_attempts` started attempts, even under repeated crashes. Prove it converges: repeatedly (a) set the entry back to `running`, (b) heal - the count climbs by exactly one each time and the task lands on `Failed` at the budget rather than being re-dispatched forever.
3. Make sure the receipt/attempt numbering stays coherent: the attempt number used for a dispatch and the number recorded on that attempt's receipt must still agree (a resumed attempt must not silently reuse a number in a way that lets `af cost` double-count the same attempt). If the reconciliation with `reap`'s existing increment needs a comment explaining who increments what and why it happens exactly once per started attempt, add it.

TEST in src/run.rs (in the existing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` - it can reach the private `heal_stale_attempt`; the helpers `running(attempts, phase)`, `settings(base)`, `cfg_with(vec![task(id)])`, `unique_base(name)` already exist):
`#[test] fn interrupted_attempt_consumes_the_retry_budget()` asserting at least:
   - a stale `running` entry with `attempts == max_attempts` (3) heals to `Failed`, NOT `Ready` - with max_attempts 3, i.e. no budget left;
   - a stale `running` entry with `attempts == 1` heals to `Ready` AND now reports `attempts == 2` - the interrupted attempt is counted;
   - the convergence property from (2): healing the same task through repeated simulated crashes climbs 1 -> 2 -> 3 and then lands on `Failed` at the budget instead of being re-dispatched indefinitely.

TESTS THAT MUST BE UPDATED (they encode the old, budget-bypassing behaviour - change them deliberately, do not delete the coverage they provide):
   - `heal_stale_attempt_reruns_unproven_agents_from_ready` in src/run.rs asserts `status["A"].attempts == 1` with the message "attempt count is preserved" and `status["B"].attempts == 2`. Under the new invariant those become 2 and 3. Keep asserting that both are rewound to `Ready` with the interrupted `last_error` and `phase == None`; only the counts change.
   - `self_heals_stale_running_state` in tests/e2e.rs seeds `run-state.json` with `{"state":"running","attempts":0,...}` and builds its worker with `worker_json(1)` (max_attempts 1). With the interrupted attempt now counted that entry has 1 attempt used out of 1 and must become Failed - so the fixture needs one more attempt of budget: use `worker_json(2)`. Keep asserting the task heals and completes and that DONE.txt is merged.
   - Check every other test that seeds a `running` entry: `restart_after_partial_run_skips_done_and_continues_remaining` (seeds `done`, unaffected), `heal_stale_attempt_agent_done_merges_without_rerunning_agent` and `mark_resumed_failure_is_terminal_only_at_max_attempts` (src/run.rs - verify they still hold under the new counts), `retry_runs_up_to_max_attempts` (an agent failure, no heal involved). The whole suite must stay green - run it.
Do not change the meaning of `max_attempts` itself (still "the maximum number of started attempts"), and do not weaken `readiness_of`/`ready_tasks` budget checks.
